problem_text:
A logistics manager is selecting cargo containers to load onto a transport vehicle. The available containers are:

* Container 1: size 17 cubic meters, revenue $84
* Container 2: size 29 cubic meters, revenue $91
* Container 3: size 14 cubic meters, revenue $132
* Container 4: size 42 cubic meters, revenue $122
* Container 5: size 35 cubic meters, revenue $19
* Container 6: size 4 cubic meters, revenue $239
* Container 7: size 32 cubic meters, revenue $179
* Container 8: size 10 cubic meters, revenue $46
* Container 9: size 4 cubic meters, revenue $34
* Container 10: size 4 cubic meters, revenue $126
* Container 11: size 26 cubic meters, revenue $145
* Container 12: size 1 cubic meter, revenue $263
* Container 13: size 17 cubic meters, revenue $61
* Container 14: size 36 cubic meters, revenue $86
* Container 15: size 6 cubic meters, revenue $199
* Container 16: size 47 cubic meters, revenue $173
* Container 17: size 41 cubic meters, revenue $277
* Container 18: size 42 cubic meters, revenue $112
* Container 19: size 35 cubic meters, revenue $118
* Container 20: size 36 cubic meters, revenue $273
* Container 21: size 20 cubic meters, revenue $278
* Container 22: size 16 cubic meters, revenue $90
* Container 23: size 12 cubic meters, revenue $191
* Container 24: size 5 cubic meters, revenue $61
* Container 25: size 19 cubic meters, revenue $222

The vehicle has a maximum capacity of 385 cubic meters. Choose the combination of containers that maximizes total revenue without exceeding this capacity limit. Each container must be either fully accepted or rejected.
